name: Seki
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir. Y. Nzang Bie. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.
sources.note: Section I.2.2.1 'Séki (B21)' (printed pp. 61-67) is a synchronic sketch taken second-hand from Gningah 2010: 7 vowels, 20 consonants, and (I.2.2.1.3, p. 66) three tonemes H, L, falling with distinctive function; tone patterns listed. Nothing on stress/accent for Seki. Part II (p. 237) has only a group-level B20 remark that theme-final syllables are regularly L, which 'pourrait conforter... une évolution vers un processus accentuel' (not Seki-specific, no stress position stated).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Seki language' (phonology tables citing Ondo-Mébiame 1986 and González Echegaray 1952).
sources.note: Consonant and vowel inventories only; nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Jacquot, André. 1983. Les classes nominales dans les langues bantoues des groupes B.10, B.20, B.30 (Gabon-Congo). Travaux et documents de l'ORSTOM 157. Paris: ORSTOM. 360 pp.
sources.note: Noun-class comparison; Seki of Cocobeach introduced pp. 70-71 and treated passim (tone-marked forms, nasal as tone bearer). No statement on stress/accent (0 hits for 'accent' in the text layer). p. 71: González Echegaray's 'baseque' of north Bata looks like a Zone A language with Fang affinities, distinct from B21 Seki.
